standard_prerequisites: Context span 792-805 (section-non-abelian preamble, shared with delivered L48308): for I finitely generated the category A of I-adically complete R-modules has cokernel of phi: M -> N given by the I-adic completion of the usual cokernel (Algebra, hathat-finitely-generated) and kernel the usual kernel, which is closed and I-adically complete by Lemma closed-is-complete (delivered card L48284)

Context span 841-859: with R = Z_p = lim Z/p^n Z and I = (p), the map diag(1, p, p^2, ...) from (direct sum of Z_p)^wedge to the product of Z_p sends (x_1, x_2, ...) with v_p(x_i) -> infinity to (x_1, p x_2, p^2 x_3, ...); the element (1, p, p^2, ...) lies in the closure of the image but not in the image; by the kernel/cokernel description this shows Im != Coim for this map
core_obligations: The category A of I-adically complete R-modules has kernels and cokernels (context: usual kernel, completed cokernel)

The context map diag(1, p, p^2, ...) over the Noetherian ring Z_p has image strictly smaller than coimage (the element (1, p, p^2, ...) is in the closure of the image, hence in the coimage-side kernel, but not in the image)
Therefore A is not abelian in general, even when R is Noetherian (Z_p is Noetherian)
proof_roadmap: Recall the kernel and cokernel formulas in A from the first context span
Instantiate the context diagonal map over Z_p
Read the Im != Coim failure off the context element (1, p, p^2, ...)
